messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: multi-gpu collective failures detected in cluster pool tp4. Severity: P1. Symptoms: repeated NCCL timeouts, container restarts, Xid events on GPU nodes. Link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/3111112222 :rotating_light:
Devon (oncall): taking it. which jobs are impacted? any customer-facing traffic? :eyes:
Alice M: seeing 502s on a handful of realtime inference endpoints, approx 8 active jobs stalled. customer-reported latency spikes ~60s then ~timeout.
Devon (oncall): ok triage plan — gather logs, attempt safe mitigations (non-disruptive) then escalate to draining if necessary. assign: Alice for logs, Emma for infra mitigations, Ben for model fallback.
Alice M: logs from pod gpu-ml-232 show repeated errors:
```
NCCL WARN Call to ncclCommInitRank timed out after 60000 ms
NCCL ERROR Unhandled async cuda error, rank 2
CUDA: Xid 79 GPU a3: GPU page fault at 0x7f...
containerd: killing process 4321 (python) due to OOM
```
Alice M: note: kernel OOMs only on 3 nodes: tp4-node-07/08/12. Others look healthy.
Emma SRE: quick mitigation options:
- try disabling IB for NCCL on affected nodes: `export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` and restart pods on node (non-disruptive if we cordon then evict)
- set `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=^lo,docker` to force sockets path if RDMA flapping suspected
- increase `--terminationGracePeriodSeconds` to allow graceful communicator teardown
I can roll a targeted evict+restart for the three nodes.
Ben L: for customer-facing endpoints we can fallback to single-GPU replica variant (lower throughput but avoids collectives). I can flip router rule to route new traffic to single-gpu model group and let ongoing multi-gpu jobs drain. Need deploy-bot to create temporary routing rule.
Caroline R: prepping node drain playbook now. steps:
1) cordon tp4-node-07
2) evict pods with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
3) set NCCL vars in node env and restart kubelet container runtime if needed
I'll do one node first to validate.
infra-bot: tp4-node-07 recent events:
- 3111112198 kernel: oom_kill invoked, process python killed
- 3111112210 nvidia-driver: Xid 79 logged
- 3111112225 containerd: container restart (exit code 137)
deploy-bot: created temporary route `model-group/safe-fallback-v1` -> single-gpu pool, weight 100 at 3111112245
Devon (oncall): do not mass-restart cluster. try node-07 patch first. Alice, capture core dumps and NCCL debug logs at `/var/log/nccl-debug.log` before and after restart.
Alice M: collecting stacks now, attaching tail of nccl logs:
```
[2026-03-15 10:02:12] NCCL INFO rank 0 -> sync barrier failed
[2026-03-15 10:02:12] NCCL INFO op allreduce stalled 0->1
[2026-03-15 10:02:13] CUDA ERROR: context already destroyed (Xid 79)
```
Ben L: initial fallback flip looks healthy, latency for new requests to single-gpu group ~stable. but backlog of existing batch jobs still stuck in collective. we'll need to kill/respawn them to restore capacity.
Emma SRE: executed `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` + pod eviction on tp4-node-07 at 3111112260. pods restarted, no immediate Xid events on that node after restart. monitoring.
Caroline R: rolling node-08 now, repeating steps. will pause between nodes for 5m.
Devon (oncall): customer comms: outreach to impacted partners (Account C + D). note that new traffic routed to fallback; some in-flight jobs may have failed. Caroline, include failure count in update.
Alice M: from core dumps: driver stack traces show DMA mapping faults; versions: nvidia 525.85, kernel 5.15. Suspect driver/firmware interaction under high TP memory pressure.
Ben L: longer term we should consider enabling model-level graceful fallback (on communicator failure switch to single rank) — but that's a runtime change. short term: continue node repairs and driver quarantining.
Emma SRE: node-08 evicted and patched, node-12 now scheduled for maintenance. no further OOMs on 07/08 after restart, metrics look better (GPU utilisation still high).
Devon (oncall): action items (so we have a clean handoff):
- Alice M: upload collected logs + core dumps to incident vault, timestamp 3111112300. include `nccl-debug.log` and `dmesg`.
- Emma SRE: continue drain on node-12 and run driver healthchecks; set `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` across pool for 2 hours to collect more traces.
- Ben L: keep fallback route until morning, coordinate with growth + solutions to inform customers.
- Caroline R: keep nodes cordoned until confirmed stable.
I'll escalate to infra lead if we see reoccurrence after 2 restarts. handing overnight to Alice M (oncall) at 3111112335. please ack.
Alice M: ack, I'll take it through the night. I'll post an update every 2h or on any regression.
Devon (oncall): thanks all, great quick coordination. summary for postmortem: multi-gpu collectives intermittently failing with driver/Xid 79 OOM signals on subset of nodes, partial mitigation via disabling IB and restarting pods; root cause likely a driver+kernel interaction with high memory pressure. next steps include driver upgrade testing, runtime graceful fallback feature, and improved alerting for repeat Xid spikes.
incident-bot: Incident record 3111112222 created. Severity set to P1. Timeline and artifacts: https://incidents.redwood.ai/3111112222/artifacts
